components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single primary action on a screen. One per view.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; height: 40px; padding: 8px 16px; background: #3b82f6; color: #f8fafc; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; border: none; border-radius: 6px; cursor: pointer; transition: background 150ms ease-out; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #2563eb; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #3b82f6; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.5; pointer-events: none; }

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: Secondary action alongside a primary button.
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; height: 40px; padding: 8px 16px; background: #ffffff; color: #0f172a; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; border: 1px solid #e2e8f0; border-radius: 6px; cursor: pointer; transition: background 150ms ease-out, border-color 150ms ease-out; } .ds-btn-outline:hover { background: #f1f5f9; border-color: #cbd5e1; } .ds-btn-outline:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #3b82f6; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Used inside tables and menus where a border would compete with content.
components.html: <button class="ds-btn-ghost"><svg width="14" height="14" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"><path d="M11 4H4a2 2 0 0 0-2 2v14a2 2 0 0 0 2 2h14a2 2 0 0 0 2-2v-7"/><path d="M18.5 2.5a2.121 2.121 0 0 1 3 3L12 15l-4 1 1-4 9.5-9.5z"/></svg> Edit</button>
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; height: 36px; padding: 4px 12px; background: transparent; color: #0f172a; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; border: none; border-radius: 6px; cursor: pointer; transition: background 150ms ease-out; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { background: #f1f5f9; } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #3b82f6; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Destructive Button
components.description: Irreversible actions only: delete member, delete semester.
components.css: .ds-btn-destructive { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; height: 40px; padding: 8px 16px; background: #ef4444; color: #f8fafc; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; border: none; border-radius: 6px; cursor: pointer; transition: background 150ms ease-out; } .ds-btn-destructive:hover { background: #dc2626; } .ds-btn-destructive:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #ef4444; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Standard form field. Focus ring is the only state change.
components.css: .ds-field { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 6px; } .ds-label { font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; color: #0f172a; } .ds-input { height: 40px; padding: 8px 12px; background: #ffffff; color: #0f172a; font-size: 0.875rem; border: 1px solid #e2e8f0; border-radius: 6px; outline: none; transition: border-color 150ms ease-out, box-shadow 150ms ease-out; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: #64748b; } .ds-input:focus { border-color: #3b82f6; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px rgba(59,130,246,0.2); } .ds-input:disabled { opacity: 0.5; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Commitment Badge
components.description: Status indicator. Always color + text. Five variants covering all commitment states.
components.html: COMMITTEDAT RISKUNCOMMITTEDNEW MEMBERLEGACY
components.css: .ds-badges { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 8px; } .ds-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; padding: 2px 10px; border-radius: 9999px; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.01em; } .ds-badge--committed { background: #dcfce7; color: #15803d; } .ds-badge--at-risk { background: #fef9c3; color: #a16207; } .ds-badge--uncommitted { background: #fee2e2; color: #b91c1c; } .ds-badge--new-member { background: #dbeafe; color: #1d4ed8; } .ds-badge--legacy { background: #fef3c7; color: #92400e; }

components.description: Full-height fixed left nav. URF Navy background. Signal Purple marks the active item.

narrative.overview:
This system is the operational equivalent of a field register kept by a community worker: every name on the page is a real person, every status reflects a real pattern of presence, every action taken here has a consequence in the community being served. The interface should feel like that register: well-organized, trustworthy, immediately readable, and free of anything that doesn't help the work.

The density is moderate. Screens hold enough information to work from without requiring constant navigation, but they don't pack data until it suffocates. Hierarchy is achieved through type weight and spatial rhythm, not color explosions or card-within-card nesting. The dark navy sidebar is the only surface that announces itself visually; everything else is calm, light, and precise.

The system rejects four things by name: the sea of identical white cards and blue buttons that defines generic SaaS products; the grey density and nested modals of legacy enterprise software; the playful gradients and bouncing animations of consumer apps; and the doves, golden gradients, and inspirational overlays of church website aesthetics.
keyCharacteristics: Light mode only; the dark sidebar is structural, not atmospheric
Hierarchy through weight contrast and spacing, not color density
Status signals always paired: color plus text, never color alone
The navy-and-purple sidebar is the single most distinctive visual element
Cards used sparingly; most content lives in tables, lists, and form layouts

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Operational Blue (#3b82f6) is the action color. It appears on primary buttons, active links, and focus rings. It does not appear as a background tint, a section color, a badge background for non-primary statuses, or a decorative highlight.

rules.name: The Sidebar Lock Rule
rules.body: URF Navy (#0f1829) is used exactly one place: the navigation sidebar. It is not a valid background for content areas, modals, tooltips, or code blocks.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: If a surface is not interactive and does not need to communicate that it floats above other content, it has no shadow. A tinted background or a 1px border is always preferred over a shadow for visual separation on static surfaces.

rules.name: The Weight Carries Rule
rules.body: With a single-family type system, hierarchy depends entirely on weight contrast. The gap between 400 (body) and 600/700 (headings) must be preserved. Never introduce a 500-weight heading at the same size as body.

dos: Do pair every status color with its text label. Color conveys category; text confirms it.
Do use weight and scale to establish hierarchy before reaching for color.
Do use #64748b (Subdued Text) for metadata, timestamps, and supporting information.
Do keep URF Navy exclusively in the sidebar.
Do use border + minimal shadow-sm to separate cards.
Do show full names before IDs in all member contexts.
Do use the ghost button variant inside tables and menus.
donts: Don't use border-left greater than 1px as a colored accent stripe on cards or list items.
Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text with a gradient fill).
Don't put decorative blur, glass, or backdrop-filter on content surfaces.
Don't make the interface look like a generic SaaS product.
Don't reference church-website visual conventions: no golden gradients, dove imagery, or congregation stock photography.
Don't design for consumer-app energy: no bouncing animations, no gamified progress bars.
Don't use URF Navy as a background for content areas, modals, or non-navigation surfaces.
Don't use Operational Blue for more than one role per screen.
Don't use Arial as the final answer — this is a known gap in the type system.
